title: Ball Dragon
paragraphs: “It started with a preemptive strike, and now they’re acting all high and mighty, demanding weapons and whatnot… but the fact that it’s all because of Bitch just makes it even more infuriating.”

Father is pointing at Takt. There’s no doubt he’s giving us the go-ahead. So I’m going to step right up. Takt and the Pope are both in fighting stances. It looks like there are quite a few of their people behind them, too.

Well, I’ve got a pretty good grasp of what needs to be taken care of here. But honestly, Takt’s attitude has me pretty pissed off, so I’m going to make sure he gets what’s coming to him. Otherwise, Ren and Itsuki won’t rest in peace.
“Well then, since I’ve gotten Father’s permission, I suppose I’ll have to take care of you lot.”
“Oink! Oink-hee!”
For some reason, Takt’s pig started squealing and pointing at me right then. What a noisy pig! How dare a pig destined for slaughter point at me?
“What!? That tone, that voice… You! Are you saying you’re Filolial Mask!?”
Oh? Does he know my ring name from Zeltoble? But why would Takt know about Filolial Mask? Just as I was pondering this, Father spoke up.
“Hey, Filolial Mask. Your true identity’s been exposed.”
That’s strange. The Filolial Mask is a secret warrior. No one should have ever seen my true identity. Soon, memories of my time in Zeltoble raced through my mind, and a certain person came to mind.
“Ah, I see. So Boldragon was actually Takt.”
If I’d killed him back then, things wouldn’t have turned out like this. Now I’ve got a plan for when the loop happens again. All I have to do is take out Takt when he shows up at the Colosseum.
“Do you know something?”
Father asked me.
“We fought several times at the Zeltoble Coliseum. I never realized it was Takt.”
“Hmm… If he’s the kind of guy who pulls stunts like this, make sure you remember him!”
“Of course.”
This was a huge blunder on my part, Motoyasu. I figured Takt was just doing his own thing around Faubrey, but it turns out he was in a place like that.

“Filolial Mask! What a surprise to run into you here! Don’t get too cocky just because you beat me in Zeltoble! Back then, you were just under the influence of that despicable debuff Magic—if I’d gone all out—”
“Gungnir X!”

Ignoring Takt’s incessant chatter, I’ll blow a hole right through the skull of his dragon—my biggest concern. The dragon’s head was pierced by the spear, its expression still one of utter contempt toward us.
The head of the dragon near Takt flew off; it collapsed, bleeding profusely, and gradually began to return to its true form. All right, then. Now we don’t have to worry about the Dragon King anymore.
“First, let’s say hello. And Takt, no matter how serious you get, you can’t beat me.”
That’s my payback for that sudden attack—which looked like a Curse Skill.
“J-just now…!?”
Takt is speechless, glancing back and forth between the dragon’s corpse and me. Well, since this is a hassle, I’ll just get it over with in one go.
“Who’s getting a little too cocky here? That’s enough of an introduction.”
Placing my hand on my spear, I utter those words for the first time in a long while. Oh? Another phrase has just popped into my mind.
“The Love Hunter commands. Holy Weapons! Servant Weapons! Answer the call of the Love Hunter, break free from the shackles of foolish power, and awaken!”
The sword and bow that had been in Takt’s hands began to glow. Then, about four more began to glow and flew toward us.
“W-what the—!? What’s going on here! Guh… I’m losing my strength! W-what the hell did you do!?”

The Holy Weapons and Seven-Star Weapons detached from Takt’s hands and began to hover around us. Takt always belts out the same line every time, doesn’t he? At this point, Father flashed a wonderful smile that sent shivers down my spine. Things are really heating up. That’s exactly how Father should be.
“‘I merely selected temporary owners so they might eventually find their rightful owners,’ was it…? Isn’t that actually describing you? You, the temporary owner.”
“Y-youuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuu!”
Oh, Takt’s rage is flaring up instantly, like an electric kettle. He’s not scary at all.
“Give it back! You thieving bastards!”
“Aren’t you the one? What do you mean, ‘rightful owner’? ‘Hero of Salvation.’ You were just a despicable bastard who stole a mere weapon, weren’t you?”
“Shut up! I’m the Chosen One!”
“Hah… It doesn’t sound very cool coming from you.”
Honestly, there’s no other way to describe this guy except as a one-trick pony. The Chosen One is Father, you know. After all, he’s the true hero who saved this world.
“How dare you kill Raildia! And to top it off, stealing my weapon—the rightful owner’s weapon—is unforgivable! Everyone! Let’s slaughter every last one of these bastards!”

Ignoring Takt as he shouts things like that, I’m about to make my move. I grab the Pope—who’s been lurking next to Takt, waiting for an opening to attack—by the collar, hurl him upward, and impale him. It seems Takt and his pig-like minions didn’t even notice I’d gotten close.
“Burst Lance X!”
“Wh-what!? G-God—”
The Pope, impaled on the tip of my spear, exploded into pieces in an instant. That’s one down, then. No, wait—since we’ve already defeated the dragon, that makes two, doesn’t it?
“What a tacky fireworks show.”
Watching the blast from Burst Lance, Father spat out those words.
“Oh my…”
“Um… we’re a little lost here. What should we do?”
“Don’t make any rash moves. It’ll be hard to protect you. At this rate, if we leave it to Motoyasu, he’ll figure something out.”
“O-okay.”

I quickly put some distance between myself and Takt, then glared at him even more fiercely. I have countless grudges against you, after all. I considered taking him out quickly, but I’d already done something dangerous that could have easily injured Filo-chan. Come to think of it, I’d hurt Filo-chan in the first world, too. I’ll never forgive you.
“W-what… that’s strength truly like a god’s.”
“We’ve been deceived… Oh, God. Please, quell your wrath.”
“Even if the Sword Heroes and Bow Heroes were impostors, the Spear Hero was the real deal.”
“And yet, in a moment of madness, we accepted a demon capable of wielding multiple holy weapons.”
“Please, forgive us.”

The three followers of the Church of the Three Heroes standing behind the Pope clasped their hands together as if in prayer. Too bad—I won’t let that slide. I’ll deal with them later. It all happened in the blink of an eye, and Takt turned to look at me, his face pale.
“I’ve already conquered this world… or have I? That’s supposed to be our line.”
Well, it was Father who truly saved the world from the Waves, but as someone who fought alongside him, I think I’m entitled to say a little something about it myself.
“What the hell are you talking about!? This strength… surely not—”
“Unfortunately, Takt, you might have an idea of what’s going on, but you’re probably wrong.”

If I recall correctly from what Father said, this guy is a reincarnated being—a subordinate of the one responsible for the “Wave.” What’s more, they’re a hopeless bunch who kill each other even among their own ranks. I’m not happy about being lumped in with the likes of him.
“Takt, was it? This guy looks like the type who’d be lurking at the summoning site for people from other worlds, waiting for them to appear.”
“That’s right. He makes sure no one stronger than himself can ever come out.”
“And you think that’ll save the world from the Wave? Is it really that simple?”
“It’s not simple at all. In fact, I’ve actually lost to the Wave once myself.”
“With an enemy so powerful that even Motoyasu—who’s this strong—can’t beat them, claiming you’ve already defeated them with something this measly? Don’t make me laugh.”
Oh, Father is seizing this opportunity to talk to me. He’s taking a dig at Takt! This is Father’s style of provocation. You can tell just how effective it is by looking at Takt’s face.
“Y-youuuuuuuuuuuuuuu! Don’t get too cockyyyyyyyyyyyyy!”
“You’ve been saying nothing but that for a while now.”
“Boo-boo-boo!”
“Give it back! That belongs to Takt!”
“It’s disgusting that you’re bringing a Filolial along! I’ll never forgive you! You thief!”
“Ha… I’ve got all the information I need now. I’m sick of talking. Motoyasu, do it.”

Father turned to me, gave a thumbs-up near his neck, and cut the connection. So, the go-ahead has finally come. Time for the cull, then. Ah, I’ve just come up with a bit of good irony to offer as a final tribute.
“Well then, Takt, if you want a holy weapon that badly, I’ll give you my spear.”
“Huh?”
“You’d better catch it properly, or things will get ugly. Now, catch it!”
Not only is that noisy pig a nuisance, but the very existence of Takt’s entourage is a scourge on the world. Above all, a disturbance has been caused, so I need to wrap this up quickly.
“Air Strike Javelin V!”
I fired an Air Strike Javelin—with a bit less power than usual—straight at Takt.
“Whoa—”

Takt dodged it by shifting his body just slightly. Well, since I fired it in a straight line, I suppose it’s no wonder he could dodge it. However, the Air Strike Javelin I fired continued flying in a straight line, and because Takt dodged, it hit the maid pig behind him and pierced right through her.
“Buh—”
“Huh…?”
With a look of utter shock, Takt looked at the maid pig that had been pierced right through, then turned to look at me.
“See? This is what happens when you don’t grab onto something.”

According to what Father told me, back in the first world, Takt also dodged attacks that ended up hitting his allies. To dodge here of all places… isn’t he a bit of an idiot? Sure, dodging means zero damage, but that’s only when there’s nothing behind you. If it’s something important, you should be able to protect it even at the cost of your own body. It’s precisely because he can’t do that on the spot that Takt isn’t a hero, I suppose.

“Y-　Aiming Lancer X! Brionac X!”

I’ll target Takt’s henchmen and the Three Heroes Cult members with the widest-range Aiming Lancer I can muster, then unleash a sweeping Brionac to vaporize them all. I’ve already taken care of any dragons that could pose a threat. There’s nothing to worry about.
“Drop dead!”
The spear I threw splits into countless fragments as it flies through the air. I’ve turned Takt’s henchmen and the Three Heroes Cultists into Swiss cheese.
“‘Gyaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!?’”
From there, the Light of Brionac sweeps them all away. Let’s wipe them out without leaving a single speck of dust.
“‘‘‘Buhiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiii!?’’’”

And it even hits Takt himself, who’s been immobilized by the Aiming Lancer. Takt isn’t showing despair or fear… he’s just staring blankly as his comrades vanish into the Light. But next, it’s your turn. I’ll just wrap Takt right up in Brionac. Eventually, perhaps finally realizing he’s in trouble, he starts screaming at the top of his lungs.
“Gyaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa――――…………”

In an instant, Takt, his entourage, and the Three Heroes cultists were all taken care of. Well, since they died in the midst of the Wave, they’ve probably become nourishment for the world. According to what Father from the First World said, I believe that’s what happens to the souls of those who die in the Wave. In that sense, they were at least somewhat useful.
“That’s about it, I guess.”
“That was insane! The spear guy really is super strong!”
Keel is sharing his thoughts excitedly. That’s right. But the strongest are Father and Filo-tan.
“Keel… seeing that massacre and still being able to say something like that—you’re the one who’s amazing.”
“Huh? Is that a problem?”
Father says to Keel with a weary expression. Well, it’s certainly exhausting to face Takt. Mentally, mostly, though.
“Um… everyone’s in a celebratory mood, but the waves aren’t over yet, are they?”
“That’s right. Since we’ve already wiped out that bunch of clowns, let’s calm the Wave down!”
“O-oh! But doesn’t this feel a bit like cleanup work?”
Keel replied to Father, tilting his head. HAHAHA. What on earth is he getting the wrong idea about? If anything, Takt is just a bonus—the Wave is the main event.
“I won’t deny it, but that was an irregular situation. I’ll have Motoyasu question them in detail later about what they were, so you guys focus on the Wave.”
“Of course! Everyone! Let’s make sure we don’t cause any casualties!”
“We Filolials will do our best not to be outdone by Keel and the gang. If we do, we’ll get a feast today.”
Luna-chan cheers on Lord Filolial in response to Keel’s rallying cry. Hearing this, Lord Filolial and the others suddenly show renewed enthusiasm and raise their voices.
“‘Woo!　Let’s go!”””
Kicking up clouds of dust, the Filolials and Keel’s group raced off to protect the nearby villages and towns. Woahhhhh! Takt kind of brought my spirits down, but I wish I’d run off with them too.
Number of heroines in Seven All – Lots
